correctness.rationale: The triangular inverse is explicit. Directly expanding its Gram characteristic polynomial gives invariant quadratic, linear and constant coefficients and a single central-weight-dependent cubic coefficient. Inverse Gram tridiagonal Jacobi simplicity gives four distinct positive endpoint roots. The horizontal-level function H has exactly three positive critical points by Rolle and Descartes; consequently all intermediate cubic coefficients retain four distinct positive roots. Differentiating their spectral moments yields the third divided difference of t^(q+2), positive because its third derivative is q(q+1)(q+2)t^(q-1)>0 for q>0. The alternating signs of the quartic derivative at ordered roots establish the individual-value behavior. The included unmodified code at verify.py was executed successfully and reproduced 216 exact rational cases; these finite checks do not prove the continuum theorem.

value.rationale: A path with fixed edge gains defines a canonical feed-forward triangular resolvent; spectral power sums measure its complete amplification profile. Dimension four is the smallest path size for which weight placement changes singular spectra. The theorem gives a natural complete sharp rearrangement classification simultaneously for all real positive exponents, and shows a nonobvious distinction between strict power-moment order and the alternating directions of individual singular values. The entire continuum result is not a routine recomputation of a single norm.
